Patients on aromatase inhibitors who develop osteoporosis are at increased risk of developing musculoskeletal symptoms and bone fracture. Taking ca/bis (calcium and vitamin B1) can reduce this risk, especially for patients receiving steroidal aromatase inhibitors or tamoxifen before starting an aromatase inhibitor. However, it's essential to note that aromatase inhibitors do not eliminate musculoskeletal symptoms in all cases.

The current evidence suggests that taking ca/bis may help mitigate the risk of osteoporosis and musculoskeletal symptoms associated with aromatase inhibitors. This is particularly important for patients who are receiving steroidal aromatase inhibitors or tamoxifen, as these medications can increase the likelihood of developing musculoskeletal issues.

To alleviate musculoskeletal symptoms, it's recommended that patients on aromatase inhibitors be offered ca/bis to reduce the incidence of osteoporosis and musculoskeletal symptoms. This may involve counseling on lifestyle modifications, such as exercise and diet, to help mitigate any potential risks associated with aromatase inhibitor use.

It is essential to consult a healthcare professional for personalized advice and treatment recommendations.
